action.question: How should I fix the missing-prefix problem?

questions.question: How should I fix the missing-prefix problem?

options.label: Re-apply now + self-heal (Recommended)
options.description: Run `titles apply` to re-prefix all drifted sessions now, AND add a periodic `titles apply` pass to the always-running supervisor loop so the platform's later auto-titling can no longer strip the prefix. Durable fix.

options.label: Re-apply now only
options.description: Run `titles apply` once to fix the current drift (idempotent). Prefixes will drift again whenever the platform re-titles a session, since nothing re-asserts them.

options.label: Self-heal mechanism only
options.description: Add the periodic supervisor pass but don't bulk-rename right now; let the periodic pass converge titles on its next ticks.

options.label: Just the diagnosis
options.description: Don't change titles or the supervisor yet — leave it with the root-cause analysis and proposed fix for you to action later.

transcript_tail.text: `familyfund → FF` is in the default map and repo detection looks sound. The likely culprit is the `set --self` command path itself. Let me read the CLI handler.

The code path looks correct (`familyfund → FF`, and `repo_from_worktree_path` resolves a FF worktree). The bug is more likely in *how the command is invoked*. Note the tension: `--self` reads the repo from `os.getcwd()` (must be the bridge worktree), but `python3 -m remote_control` needs the `remote_control` module importable from that cwd. Let me test from this FamilyFund worktree:

Both the import and the resolution work perfectly from here — `[FF] #82 …` is exactly what `set --self` would produce. So the logic isn't broken. Let me look at the *actual live session titles* to see what's really happening — read-only dry run, filtered to FamilyFund:

Now I can see the real pattern. There are **two kinds** of FamilyFund sessions:

- **Properly prefixed** (`=`, already correct): `[FF] #27 …`, `[FF] #81 …`, `[FF] #78 …`, `[FF] #77 …` — start-work worked.
- **Unprefixed, auto-described** (`~`, would be renamed): e.g. `'Defense-in-depth ACL scoping for fund controllers'` (that's #85's work), `'Cross-account data visibility issue'`, `'Testpool DB rotation'`.

That first `~` example is the smoking gun: a session clearly doing **#85's** work but titled with a generic *platform-generated* summary and **no `[FF]` prefix** — meaning the title `set` by `start-work` got **overwritten by the platform's automatic title generation** that fires later in the session. The code itself is fine (I verified it emits `[FF] #85 …`); the platform clobbers it afterward.

Let me confirm there's no existing self-healing pass and see where one would live:

Confirmed: **there is no self-healing pass.** `start-work` sets the title once at claim time, and the platform's later auto-titling overwrites it — nothing re-applies the `[FF]` prefix afterward. That's the bug.

Let me check the supervisor's loop structure so a durable fix can hook into it:

Root cause confirmed. Here's the diagnosis:

**The `start-work` title code works** — I verified it emits exactly `[FF] #N …` from a FamilyFund worktree. The problem is **nothing re-asserts it**: `start-work` sets the title once at claim time, then the platform's automatic title-generation fires later in the session and overwrites it, dropping the `[FF]` prefix. There's no periodic self-healing pass anywhere (not in the supervisor, no cron). That's why some sessions kept `[FF] #N` (claim settled after auto-title) while others drifted to bare summaries like *"Defense-in-depth ACL scoping for fund controllers"* (#85's session).

The dry-run also shows ~15 FamilyFund sessions currently drifted (and more across other repos). How do you want to fix it?
